output.summary: A genus of broad-leaved flowering perennials native to tropical and subtropical Asia and eastern Australia, Alocasia grows from rhizomes or tubers. Its large heart- or arrow-shaped leaves often hide the inconspicuous flowers. Corms of some species can be processed for food, but raw plants contain irritants and ingestion may remain dangerous despite precautions.
output.edibilityNote: Corms of some species can be processed as food; raw plants irritate the mouth and throat, and ingestion may remain dangerous despite prolonged boiling.
